newsitem.title: LATVIA: Latvian stock market to increase trading days.
newsitem.headline: Latvian stock market to increase trading days.

text.p: Latvia's stock market plans to start trading four days a week later this month, stock exchange president Uldis Cerps said on Tuesday.
The market, which has a capitalisation of some 77 million lats, began with one session a week in the middle of last year.
It has gradually been increasing the number of trading days to the current three on Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday.
"December 20 is the first Friday on which we will have a session," Cerps told a news conference, announcing the new trading day.
He said that the exchange was losing some business to off-market trade and hoped to bring it back to the bourse.
The most popular share on the market is Unibanka, one of the top banks, but it also has an active secondary market.
Unibanka was earlier today joined on the official bourse by leading confectionery maket, Staburadze.
Estonia is the only Baltic market which currently trades five times a week.
